lots.guide_summary: All surviving evidence is SOLD (dated US eBay completed sales shown on PriceCharting, new-in-box condition, last 24 months); no UNSOLD or ASKING entries kept. Lot-level range: A$110 = sum of the lowest NIB sale per figure (US$76.72), A$331 = sum of the median NIB sale per figure (US$230.40), both at US$1 = A$1.4383. About two thirds of the value is the Deadpool (median about US$105 over 24 months, US$150 typical in 2026). US prices, so Australian resale may differ.
lots.working: Keep: lowest same-item NIB sold per figure, last 24 months (USD): Batman 4.99, Beast Man 9.00, Deadpool 26.00, Erlich 6.99, Predator 0.99, Interplanetary Batman 5.00, Kramer Golf 2.25, Kramer Good Cop 4.50, Okoye 3.50, Pajama Jack 2.50, Snoopy 11.00 = US$76.72 x 1.4383 = A$110.34; / 1.198 = A$92.10, round down to $90. Flip: likely resale = sum of 24-month median NIB sales US$230.40 x 1.4383 = A$331; less eBay AU fees about 13.4% plus A$0.30 per order x 11 = about A$48; postage charged to buyers, packaging about A$2 x 11 = A$22; net about A$261 / 2.396 = A$108.9, round down to $105. All-in at $90 hammer = A$107.82; at $105 = A$125.79. Pickup Moonah, inbound freight $0.
lots.confidence_reason: Box numbers and convention stickers read in the photo and each figure has several dated sales on PriceCharting pages I opened, but they are US eBay sales seen through an aggregator (eBay item pages not opened), and box condition (which drives Funko value) is not inspected.
lots.dropped_entries: Dropped all 11 researcher PriceCharting entries as filed: they were aggregate guide values (not single prices paid) filed as ASKING, and the researcher mislabelled PriceCharting's middle column as 'complete in box' when for Funko it means 'In Dmg Box' (figure in damaged box), so the A$235 total understated an undamaged-box lot. Replaced with dated individual NIB completed sales from the same pages, filed as SOLD. Excluded from the stats: chase, Target, FYE, Amazon, NYCC-only, invisible/red/chrome variants, multi-figure sets, damaged or 'not mint' boxes, and loose figures. Also corrected: Snoopy sticker reads 2016 Summer Convention (not a generic exclusive sticker).
lots.key_photo_findings: Single photo, 11 boxes stacked, numbers and stickers legible: Deadpool 112 with 2016 Summer Convention sticker (white suit figure visible), Snoopy 139 and Pajama Jack 205 with 2016 Summer Convention stickers, Batman 188 and Interplanetary Batman 196 with 2017 Summer Convention stickers, Predator 620 and Okoye 385 with Fall Convention stickers, Beast Man 539 flocked with Fall Convention sticker, both Kramers with Popcultcha stickers, Erlich 432 no sticker. Front faces look clean; no protectors; backs, tops and corners not visible.
lots.condition: Boxed, fronts appear clean and uncreased in the photo; corners, backs and window film not seen. Unknown whether stickers are original.
lots.question_for_gowans: Please check the box corners, backs and windows for creases, crushing or sun fade, especially the Deadpool #112, and whether any figure has been taken out of its box.

lots.confidence_reason: Model read clearly on the fascia, but all evidence is European asking prices for what may be a different generation; no sales; untested.
lots.dropped_entries: Dropped PLN 499 Sprzedajemy listing: it bundles an ST-40 tuner, so not comparable. Dropped Vendora EUR 150 listing: it is the 74PM30/02B, a different (Philips-era) model. Kept the others but downgraded from 'close' to 'category guide' because the European PM-30 (2x35W, sold with ST-40) does not appear to be this mic-mixing console model.
lots.key_photo_findings: Fascia reads 'PM 30' in script, 'marantz' and 'console Stereo amplifier'. Controls: selector (phono/tuner/aux), tape monitor, bass and treble sliders, source mixing knob, stepped volume, phones, 20Hz low filter, mono, balance slider, mic jack, loudness, power. Brushed black panel with scratches and reflections; selector knob face scuffed; no rear view, so no serial, voltage or condition of terminals seen.
lots.condition: Cosmetically fair to good from the front, knob scuffs and panel scratches; untested; rear and internals not seen.
lots.question_for_gowans: Does it power on and pass sound on both channels? What voltage and serial number are on the rear label, and are the rear terminals and power cord intact?

lots.what_it_is: Round mahogany-cased dial wall clock, about 12 inch white dial with Roman numerals, broad arrow (government property mark) above centre and issue number 81 below, single winding hole (timepiece), hinged bezel. Likely government or railway office issue, maker and authority unknown.
lots.guide_summary: Nothing survives: the researcher found no entries and my own searches were refused (web search budget exhausted); a plain Bing fetch returned irrelevant results. No sold, unsold or asking evidence.
lots.working: No SOLD evidence, so no maximum bid.
lots.confidence_reason: Broad arrow and number read in the photo, but no maker, movement or authority seen, the minute hand looks broken, and there is no market evidence at all.
lots.key_photo_findings: Enlarged crops: broad arrow above centre and '81' below the winding hole look painted as part of the dial, not later additions, but cannot be proven from the photo. Only the hour hand (hoop type, pointing near X) is on the arbor; a broken piece of hand appears loose behind the glass at VI, so the minute hand is broken or missing. Small paint loss on the dial edge near VII; dial discoloured and grubby; bezel hinge at the right, glass present. Case shows wear but looks sound. Movement, back and any maker stamp not visible.
lots.condition: Dial discoloured with small paint loss, minute hand broken or detached, running condition unknown, movement unseen.
lots.question_for_gowans: Is the minute hand broken (there seems to be a loose piece behind the glass)? Is there a maker's name or broad arrow stamped on the movement or case, is it a fusee movement, and does it come with a key and run?
